name: Zephaniah
title: Levite Who Sealed the Covenant
summary: Zephaniah was a Levite who lived in the post-exilic period and was active in the spiritual renewal work under Nehemiah. He participated in public prayer and confession to God, and was among those who sealed the covenant of faithfulness to the Lord's law. The name Zephaniah is borne by several individuals in the Old Testament, but the most prominent are associated with worship and covenant-making during Nehemiah's time.

keyEvents.title: Public Prayer and Confession
keyEvents.description: Zephaniah was among the Levites who cried out with a loud voice to the Lord their God during the great gathering of prayer and fasting in Jerusalem.

keyEvents.title: Praise and Worship
keyEvents.description: Zephaniah took part in leading the people in praise and worship, where they confessed God's greatness and his faithfulness throughout Israel's history.

keyEvents.title: Sealing the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Zephaniah was one of the Levites who placed his seal on the written covenant in which the people committed themselves to follow God's law.

keyEvents.title: Covenant Promises Concerning God's Law
keyEvents.description: Zephaniah and the others who sealed the covenant committed themselves to keep God's commands, statutes, and laws, and not to give their daughters in marriage to the surrounding peoples.

keyEvents.title: Priestly service in the temple
keyEvents.description: A Zephaniah is mentioned among the priests who blew trumpets at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall under Nehemiah's leadership.
